How does the SCRIPE CRM Enterprise Overhaul achieve Sovereign Assignee Lookup, Zero-Offset Direct Kanban Drag, Dynamic Stage Gates, and 5-Layer OWASP Defense?

Long image

A

Answer

SCRIPE CRM Enterprise Overhaul unifies tenant-scoped sovereign assignee lookup with field-level redaction, eliminates Broken Object Level Authorization (BOLA) across lead, opportunity, and buying committee handlers, replaces legacy drag handles with high-precision full-card @dnd-kit pointer tracking, binds stage progression to an audited exit-gate allowlist with dynamic custom fields, and enforces real-time multi-currency conversion across Kanban headers, 360 views, and financial reports.1

  1. Tenant-scoped assignee endpoint GET /api/v1/crm/settings/assignees queries active users and teams with AES-GCM encrypted wire IDs and masks PII when identity/email fields are restricted.1
  2. PermittedExitFieldKeys and MoveOpportunityStageCommandHandler enforce strict allowlists for exit gates, eliminating unchecked string keys and verifying tenant context on every stage transition.2
  3. KanbanSortableCard and CrmEntitySearchSelect achieve zero-handle direct full-card drag with a 6px PointerSensor constraint, inline quick-create dialogs, and instant multi-currency header aggregation.3
  4. Buying committee stakeholder management (CrmDealContactRole), CrmWorkflowTransitionDialog reset-on-open lifecycle, and batch display-name hydration deliver complete parity with Odoo 18, SAP Sales Cloud, and Salesforce Lightning.4

How do Direct Full-Card Kanban Drag and Searchable Entity Combobox interact with Stage Gate Overlays?

Diagram structure
  • CRM Kanban View kanban_view
  • KanbanSortableCard sortable_card
  • 6px PointerSensor sensor
  • KanbanStageColumn drop_column
  • CrmEntitySearchSelect search_select
  • Inline QuickCreate quick_create
  • TransitionDialog gate_dialog
  • useCrmCurrency currency_hook
  • CRM API Gateway api_service
  • kanban_view → sortable_card · renders cards
  • sortable_card → sensor · pointer drag
  • sensor → drop_column · tracks drop target
  • sortable_card → gate_dialog · triggers gate
  • gate_dialog → search_select · entity input
  • search_select → quick_create · fallback create
  • search_select → api_service · debounced lookup
  • drop_column → currency_hook · column total sum
  • gate_dialog → api_service · stage move commit

In high-velocity enterprise sales environments, drag handles such as GripVertical introduce interaction friction, while unconstrained pointer events cause accidental dragging during text selection or button clicking. Furthermore, hardcoded entity pickers and static UUID mocks degrade both user trust and security boundaries. SCRIPE CRM re-engineers Kanban interaction by attaching @dnd-kit/sortable listeners directly to the outer matte card container, configuring a 6px PointerSensor activation distance, isolating button pointer events via stopPropagation(), and integrating CrmEntitySearchSelect for server-backed, debounced entity search with inline quick-creation.3

  1. Zero-Handle Direct Drag ↗

    KanbanSortableCard spreads sortable attributes and listeners directly onto the root card element, eliminating the legacy GripVertical icon button while keeping resting card borders flat matte without double-nested border wrappers.

  2. 6px Pointer Distance Constraint ↗

    PointerSensor enforces an activation constraint of 6px distance, preventing accidental card drags during clicks, double-clicks, or text selections; inner action buttons invoke stopPropagation() on pointer down.

  3. Server-Searchable Entity Combobox ↗

    CrmEntitySearchSelect performs debounced 250ms asynchronous queries against tenant-scoped endpoints (assignees, accounts, contacts, leads), rendering human display names and subtitles while maintaining encrypted IDs internally.

  4. Inline Entity Quick-Create ↗

    When a required account or contact is absent, users create the record directly inside CrmEntityQuickCreateDialog without leaving the transition screen or losing in-flight form data.

  5. Form Reset on Open Lifecycle ↗

    CrmWorkflowTransitionDialog executes reset(defaultValues) upon opening or record switching, guaranteeing that stale form state from previous transitions never contaminates new stage moves.

Drag Gesture Model
Direct full-card draggable surface; cursor-grab active:cursor-grabbing; 0 GripVertical handles
Activation Constraint
PointerSensor with distance: 6 (or 8px); zero jitter on click; stopPropagation() on card footer CTAs
Entity Search & Pick
CrmEntitySearchSelect with 250ms debounce; supports assignee, account, contact, lead, opportunity
Quick-Create Flow
In-situ modal creation via CrmEntityQuickCreateDialog; automatically selects newly created entity
Concurrency Token
Form submission transmits ExpectedRowVersion; conflicts trigger HTTP 409 and prompt user refresh

How does Tenant-Scoped Assignee Lookup enforce Field Redaction and prevent BOLA attacks?

Diagram structure
  • Search Select client
  • Settings API ctrl
  • Assignee Handler handler
  • Field Resolver pbac
  • Id Encryption crypto
  • User Repo repo
  • client → ctrl · GET /assignees?search=sarah&kind=user
  • ctrl → handler · LookupCrmAssigneesQuery
  • handler → pbac · GetRestrictedFieldsAsync("users")
  • pbac → handler · Restricted fields: ["email"]
  • handler → repo · SearchActiveUsersAsync(tenantId, "sarah")
  • repo → handler · Active Tenant Users
  • handler → crypto · Encrypt(user.Id)
  • crypto → handler · AES-GCM Cipher Token
  • handler → ctrl · Result.Success(AssigneeDto)
  • ctrl → client · 200 OK [{ id: "enc_...", displayName: "Sarah Chen" }]

Exposing unbounded user lists across multi-tenant boundaries creates severe privacy and security vulnerabilities (OWASP API1:2023 BOLA and API3:2023 Broken Object Property Level Authorization). SCRIPE CRM implements sovereign assignee resolution via GET /api/v1/crm/settings/assignees, routed to LookupCrmAssigneesQueryHandler. The handler enforces tenant isolation via _currentUser.EffectiveTenantId, verifies caller CRM permissions (crm.overview.read, crm.records.assign, etc.), evaluates field-level masking via IRestrictedFieldsResolver, and encrypts all outbound entity identifiers using IIdEncryptionService. Additionally, all mutation handlers verify parent opportunity and tenant matching before modifying records.1

  1. Tenant Authentication & Scope ↗

    The handler verifies that EffectiveTenantId is present and non-empty; missing or invalid tenant context immediately yields 403 Forbidden (CRM_TENANT_CONTEXT_REQUIRED).

  2. Granular CRM PBAC Verification ↗

    Callers must possess one of 8 permitted CRM scopes (crm.overview.read, crm.records.assign, crm.activities.followup, etc.) unless operating as a System Protected Admin.

  3. Dynamic Restricted Fields Masking ↗

    IRestrictedFieldsResolver checks whether firstName, lastName, username, or email are restricted for the caller's role; restricted identity fields abort the candidate read, while restricted email omits email from subtitles.

  4. Symmetric Wire ID Encryption ↗

    Candidate GUIDs are passed through _idEncryption.Encrypt(candidate.Id) so raw database database keys are never exposed on the wire.

  5. Human-Readable Client Selection ↗

    CrmEntitySearchSelect renders the sanitized displayName and subtitle (role/department) in the popover while storing the opaque encrypted token in the form state.

OWASP API1:2023 BOLA Mitigation Across Handlers

In addition to the assignee lookup, all CRM mutation handlers (MoveOpportunityStageCommandHandler, AddDealContactRoleCommandHandler, RemoveDealContactRoleCommandHandler, ConvertLeadCommandHandler) verify that both the target record and any child entities belong strictly to EffectiveTenantId. When a record does not exist or belongs to another tenant, the backend emits a uniform 404 NotFound, preventing tenant enumeration attacks.

How do Dynamic Pipeline Stage Gates and Buying Committee Roles govern Deal Progression?

Diagram structure
  • BANT Qualification lead_qual
  • Convert to Deal lead_convert
  • Drag / Advance Stage opp_move
  • Check Permitted Keys check_allowlist
  • Validate Required Inputs validate_fields
  • Primary Stakeholder Set? check_committee
  • Won or Lost Move? terminal_check
  • Won: Close Notes terminal_win
  • Lost: Reason Code terminal_loss
  • check_allowlist → validate_fields · keys permitted
  • check_committee → terminal_check · committee valid
  • lead_convert → opp_move · creates deal
  • lead_qual → lead_convert · qualified
  • opp_move → check_allowlist · triggers gate
  • terminal_check → terminal_loss · lost stage
  • terminal_check → terminal_win · won stage
  • validate_fields → check_committee · inputs valid

Enterprise sales cycles demand that stage movements satisfy strict governance criteria before advancing toward financial commitment. Legacy implementations suffered from arbitrary string dictionary keys and unchecked client payloads. SCRIPE CRM establishes PermittedExitFieldKeys as a sovereign allowlist governing exit gates across both Lead and Opportunity pipelines. When moving an opportunity into advanced stages (Solution Fit, Proposal, Negotiation), the system validates required fields (estimatedAmount, targetCloseDate, solutionFitConfirmed, primaryContactRole), verifies buying committee stakeholders (CrmDealContactRole), and prompts for loss or disqualification reasons upon terminal closure.2

  1. BANT Lead Qualification ↗

    Leads are scored against Budget, Authority, Need, and Timeline criteria; qualifying moves validate leadPhoneOrEmail, leadSourceChannel, and leadBantNotes.

  2. Atomic Deal & Party Conversion ↗

    ConvertLeadCommandHandler transitions the lead to Qualified, creates or links the CrmAccountPartyRef and CrmContactPartyRef, and scaffolds the initial CrmOpportunity with initial stage and assigned owner.

  3. Permitted Exit Field Allowlist ↗

    PermittedExitFieldKeys.All validates incoming field dictionary keys; custom attributes must match approved prefixes (custom:, rule:, action:, restrict:, validate:).

  4. Dynamic Gate Field Validation ↗

    Handlers check required commercial bounds (estimatedAmount > 0, targetCloseDate >= UtcNow, solutionFitConfirmed == true); unfulfilled gates block progression or display CrmWorkflowTransitionDialog.

  5. Buying Committee Governance ↗

    Critical pipeline transitions require at least one verified stakeholder contact role (DecisionMaker, EconomicBuyer, TechnicalEvaluator, Champion) registered via CrmDealContactRole.

  6. Terminal Outcome Enforcement ↗

    Moving to Closed Won enforces mandatory close notes and verified accounts; moving to Closed Lost requires a structured lossReasonCode (Pricing, Competitor, BudgetCut, NoDecision).

How does the CRM Physical Database Schema maintain Cross-Module Integrity and Concurrency?

To support high-throughput operations across multi-tenant sport enterprises, SCRIPE CRM enforces Clean Architecture 3-project boundaries with zero cross-module EF Core foreign keys. Inter-module references to PartyKernel and Identity use logical GUID identifiers. Concurrency is managed via optimistic locking tokens (RowVersion / xmin), while all tables inherit from AuditableEntity<Guid> (CreatedAt, CreatedBy, UpdatedAt, UpdatedBy, IsDeleted).4

Diagram structure
  • Leads crm_leads
  • Opportunities crm_opportunities
  • Buying Committee crm_deal_contact_roles
  • Account Party Refs crm_account_party_refs
  • crm_deal_contact_roles → crm_opportunities
  • crm_opportunities → crm_account_party_refs
Persistence Architecture
Dual-Mode isolated schema (crm.*); zero cross-module foreign key constraints
Optimistic Concurrency
RowVersion byte-array / xmin token on all entities; guarded in CQRS commands
Display Name Hydration
CrmDisplayNameResolutionHelper batches accounts, contacts, and users with 0 N+1 queries
Soft Delete Support
IsDeleted boolean flag indexed with TenantId on all auditable entities
Indexing Strategy
Composite indexes on (TenantId, StageKey, IsDeleted) and (TenantId, OwnerUserId, IsDeleted)

How does the Multi-Currency Engine convert deals across Kanban Columns and Financial Reports?

Sports enterprise franchises frequently negotiate sponsorships, facility bookings, and player transfers in diverse currencies (SAR, USD, EUR, GBP, AED). Without unified multi-currency aggregation, pipeline totals become mathematically invalid when mixed currencies are summed naively. SCRIPE CRM implements useCrmCurrency on the client and server-side rate snapshots in ICrmSettingsStore. When all opportunities in a column share the same currency, the column header displays that native currency; when opportunities have mixed currencies, the engine converts each deal into the tenant's BaseCurrency using real-time cached exchange rates.3
